277108840_6ed71f39.text: In both male and female mice, the expression of Kiss1 in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus was robust, with this neuronal population showing expression of Tac2 and prodynorphin (Pdyn) as has been previously reported, and Slc17a6 but not Slc32a1, denoting glutamatergic functionality. Estrogen receptor α was highly and the androgen receptor partially expressed in these neurons, and gonadectomy significantly reduced Kiss1 expression in the arcuate nucleus in both sexes
277108840_6ed71f39.section: Cell identity, neurotransmitter phenotype, and neurochemical features

277108840_673e7bb6.text: .In agreement with previous reports in mice [17, 21], our ISH analyses showed very high co-expression of Kiss1 in the ARC with Tac2 ( �92%– 95%) and Pdyn ( �95%– 97%) in both sexes (Figures 3 and 4), and approximately 84%–95% co-expression of Kiss1 and Slc17a6 mRNAs, which identify these cells as excitatory glutamatergic neurons (Figure 5A–D). In contrast, no co-expression of Kiss1 with Slc32a1, the gene coding for the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA transporter, was observed in either sex (Figure 5E–H). This confirms that ARC Kiss1 neurons in mice, also known as KNDy neurons, are glutamatergic and not GABAergic [24]
277108840_673e7bb6.section: Cell identity, neurotransmitter phenotype, and neurochemical features

277108840_36cfe5a6.text: .In line with previous studies [7, 23], the ARC population in male and female mice showed robust expression of Esr1 (male: 97%; female: 99%), but lower expression of Ar mRNA (male: 52%; female: 54%) (Figures 7–9), with no sex differences in this expression pattern
277108840_36cfe5a6.section: Cell identity, neurotransmitter phenotype, and neurochemical features

277108840_aa86ce60.text: .The present data support previous findings [17] 21] indicating that the vast majority of Kiss1 neurons in the arcuate nucleus express both Tac2 and Pdyn and are glutamatergic but not GABAergic. These findings further support the concept that hypothalamic Kiss1 neurons are heterogeneous and emphasize that Kiss1 cell populations in the mouse brain can be distinguished based on the expression of the neuropeptides, sex steroid receptors and classical neurotransmitters shown in this report.
